profiles.default: small deterministic populations; the same code path plain `npm test` runs; an explicit unknown profile name is refused, not silently treated as default
profiles.full: real production ceilings: the 16 MiB structural query boundary, a near-structural-limit committed population against the 128 MiB index budget, the physical 100000-entry scan boundary with the MCP runtime WORKSPACE rejection before any catalogue or inference call, pinned pi-v0.19.0 old/new writer processes and the recovery drill with both documented offline choices

scenarios: q1 committed run-store growth curve (default: 4 and 16 runs; full adds 64, 256 and 1024)
q2a exact structural-limit query boundaries (full only)
q2b near-structural-limit population reaching the real secondary-index budget; writer and reader refusals (full only)
q3 repeated corrupt-index reads, writer repair, distinct valid-but-incomplete case
q4 physical 100000-entry scan cap boundary plus the MCP runtime WORKSPACE rejection with a denied counting transport (full only)
q5 pinned pi-v0.19.0 and current writer processes on one parent
q6 non-destructive recovery drill; unchanged-old-cache-plus-new-cacheDir and whole-cache-rename offline choices
plan.footprintEstimate: planning estimate only, replaced by measured numbers in summary.json: default well under 100 MB and cleaned on success; full retains every dataset in owned encrypted scratch after success (bounded, roughly 1 to 2 GiB per run including preserved index copies)

note: Single-host observations on the recorded mount. Byte counts are filesystem sizes; elapsed values are wall-clock milliseconds. No heap cap, latency promise or unsupported-platform claim follows from them.
